pmc.title: Fitness · fatigue · form
pmc.aria: Fitness and fatigue lines with form bars over the last {n} days
pmc.tip:
Fitness, fatigue and form over the last {n} days (switch to 7, 42 or 90 days next to the title; the choice is remembered).
How to read: blue = fitness (42-day average load), orange = fatigue (7 days); bars = form = yesterday's fitness − fatigue, coloured by form ÷ fitness: red < −30% High Risk, green −30 to −10% Optimal, light purple −10 to +5% grey zone, purple +5 to +25% Fresh, yellow > +25% Transition.
Look for: blue rising = getting fitter; orange above blue = training more than usual lately; negative form is not bad.
Method: the Banister model, as applied to power training by Coggan; bands from Friel, rules of thumb, a direction only. Other platforms often call these CTL, ATL and TSB.
Load is on the same scale as TrainingPeaks' TSS® (one hour at threshold = 100), so the numbers are roughly comparable, but details differ (e.g. moving time only, a climbing bonus), so they will not match exactly. TSS® is a registered trademark of TrainingPeaks, LLC.
thr.wait_cool: The LTHR test is more accurate once it cools down (you can still schedule it now)
drift.basis_power: HR drift from power (power ÷ HR, Pw:HR)
drift.basis_pace: HR drift from pace (speed ÷ HR, Pa:HR)
z5.title: Zone 3 / Zone 5 unlock tracks
split.title: Intensity distribution
split.tip:
Moving time of this period's endurance activities, split into three heart-rate bands.
How to read: low < AeT, moderate AeT–LTHR, high ≥ LTHR; bar length = share.
Look for: 75% low intensity is the floor, 80% the target (≥ 90% in base); this is a reminder, not a condition for unlocking Zone 3.
Method: Seiler 2006.
